docs/ir-spec.md Â§10-tier.

`Pl::RegexTier::tier(PATTERN, FLAGS)` answers `native` / `pcre` / `refused`,
plus `dynamic` when the pattern is not known at compile time (an interpolated
one) -- a DECLARED absence, never a guess.  It is a single left-to-right scan
tracking exactly two states a construct test can be fooled by: a backslash
escape and a bracketed character class.

THE ONE BUG IT HAD, and the reason `}`-possessive needs the counted test:
`\p{L}+` read its `}+` as a possessive quantifier and called every `\p{â¦}+`
pattern `pcre`.  The `}` arm now scans back to the matching `{` and requires
`{n}` / `{n,}` / `{n,m}`.  31 probes in the module's own test path.

RULED HERE (and stated in the spec): an unrecognised MODIFIER letter answers
`pcre`, not an error.  Rule 12's die boundary (DECIDED s329) is "die when the
missing case produces a value the program consumes"; nothing here reaches the
program, so the conservative answer -- "this target needs the bigger engine" --
is right and a wrong `native` would be the harmful one.

THIS TARGET IGNORES THE TIER: cl-ppcre runs everything cl-ppcre runs and the
keyword is read and discarded by the macro.  What it buys is that
`pl2cl --manifest`'s `needs.regex.tier` stops printing the word `unclassified`
and prints a histogram over the four classes, each present with a zero
(ir-spec Â§10b; the stale manifest-01.t row was repaired in the same commit).
